title: Dasakam 62 — Indrayajñanirodhana and Govardhanayāga
description: Krishna redirects Vraja from Indra’s annual sacrifice toward Govardhana and the Brahmins; Indra’s pride turns toward a storm, while the cowherds trust in protection.
translation_note: No sourced English verse translation was supplied or added; translation_en remains empty pending editorial review. Captions are commentary, not translations.

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदाचिद्गोपालान् विहितमखसम्भारविभवान्
निरीक्ष्य त्वं शौरे मघवमदमुद्ध्वंसितुमनाः ।
विजानन्नप्येतान् विनयमृदु नन्दादिपशुपा-
नपृच्छः को वायं जनक भवतामुद्यम इति ॥ ६२-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadācidgōpālān vihitamakhasaṁbhāravibhavān
nirīkṣya tvaṁ śaurē maghavamadamudhvaṁsitumanāḥ |
vijānannapyētān vinayamr̥du nandādipaśupā-
napr̥cchaḥ kō vāyaṁ janaka bhavatāmudyama iti || 62-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Once the Gopas were arranging pooja for Indra and started to collect materials for it. Krishna decided to humble the pride of Indra. So Krishna in all humility and politeness asked his father Nanda and gopas, the reason for this effort.

stanzas.sanskrit:
बभाषे नन्दस्त्वां सुत ननु विधेयो मघवतो
मखो वर्षे वर्षे सुखयति स वर्षेण पृथिवीम् ।
नृणां वर्षायत्तं निखिलमुपजीव्यं महितले
विशेषादस्माकं तृणसलिलजीवा हि पशवः ॥ ६२-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
babhāṣē nandastvāṁ suta nanu vidhēyō maghavatō
makhō varṣē varṣē sukhayati sa varṣēṇa pr̥thivīm |
nr̥ṇāṁ varṣāyattaṁ nikhilamupajīvyaṁ mahitalē
viśēṣādasmākaṁ tr̥ṇasalilajīvā hi paśavaḥ || 62-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Nanda Maharaj told that a yagya has to be performed for Indra every year as He gives rain to the earth which is essential for all human beings, cattle and for growing green pastures.

stanzas.sanskrit:
इति श्रुत्वा वाचं पितुरयि भवानाह सरसं
धिगेतन्नो सत्यं मघवजनिता वृष्टिरिति यत् ।
अदृष्टं जीवानां सृजति खलु वृष्टिं समुचितां
महारण्ये वृक्षाः किमिव बलिमिन्द्राय ददते ॥ ६२-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
iti śrutvā vācaṁ piturayi bhavānāha sarasaṁ
dhigētannō satyaṁ maghavajanitā vr̥ṣṭiriti yat |
adr̥ṣṭaṁ jīvānāṁ sr̥jati khalu vr̥ṣṭiṁ samucitāṁ
mahāraṇyē vr̥kṣāḥ kimiva balimindrāya dadatē || 62-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna sweetly refused the above statement of Nanda and said that the rain is not given by Indra. It happens due to past actions of the living beings. He further pointed out that in the big forest, the trees do not offer anything to Indra for rain.

stanzas.sanskrit:
इदं तावत् सत्यं यदिह पशवो नः कुलधनं
तदाजीव्यायासौ बलिरचलभर्त्रे समुचितः ।
सुरेभ्योऽप्युत्कृष्टा ननु धरणिदेवाः क्षितितले
ततस्तेऽप्याराध्या इति जगदिथ त्वं निजजनान् ॥ ६२-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
idaṁ tāvatsatyaṁ yadiha paśavō naḥ kuladhanaṁ
tadājīvyāyāsau baliracalabhartrē samucitaḥ |
surēbhyō:’pyutkr̥ṣṭā nanu dharaṇidēvāḥ kṣititalē
tatastē:’pyārādhyā iti jagaditha tvaṁ nijajanān || 62-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna then, explained that it is Govardhana hill which is giving the green pastures and water to the cows. Therefore to have prosperity it is necessary that Gopas pray to Govardhana Hill and worship the learned holy Brahmins who are even greater than Devas.

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवद्वाचं श्रुत्वा बहुमतियुतास्तेऽपि पशुपाः
द्विजेन्द्रानर्चन्तो बलिमददुरुच्चैः क्षितिभृते ।
व्यधुः प्रादक्षिण्यं सुभृशमनमन्नादरयुता-
स्त्वमादः शैलात्मा बलिमखिलमाभीरपुरतः ॥ ६२-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavadvācaṁ śrutvā bahumatiyutāstē:’pi paśupāḥ
dvijēndrānarcantō balimadaduruccaiḥ kṣitibhr̥tē |
vyadhuḥ prādakṣiṇyaṁ subhr̥śamanamannādarayutā-
stvamādaḥ śailātmā balimakhilamābhīrapurataḥ || 62-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Hearing Krishna's words, Nandagopan and the gopas then honoured the learned Brahmins and performed yagnya and offerings and prostrated to the Govardhana Hill with great reverence. Krishna himself became the soul of the mountain and accepted all the pooja and offerings

stanzas.sanskrit:
अवोचश्चैवं तान् किमिह वितथं मे निगदितं
गिरीन्द्रो नन्वेष स्वबलिमुपभुङ्क्ते स्ववपुषा ।
अयं गोत्रो गोत्रद्विषि च कुपिते रक्षितुमलं
समस्तानित्युक्ता जहृषुरखिला गोकुलजुषः ॥ ६२-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
avōcaścaivaṁ tānkimiha vitathaṁ mē nigaditaṁ
girīndrō nanvēṣa svabalimupabhuṅktē svavapuṣā |
ayaṁ gōtrō gōtradviṣi ca kupitē rakṣitumalaṁ
samastānityuktā jahr̥ṣurakhilā gōkulajuṣaḥ || 62-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna told the gopas that Govardhana hill personally accepted all of their offerings. Even if Indra got angry with gopas, the mountain will protect them from his anger. The Gopas were happy to hear this and went back home along with Krishna.

stanzas.sanskrit:
परिप्रीता याताः खलु भवदुपेता व्रजजुषो
व्रजं यावत् तावन्निजमखविभङ्गं निशमयन् ।
भवन्तं जानन्नप्यधिकरजसाऽऽक्रान्तहृदयो
न सेहे देवेन्द्रस्त्वदुपरचितात्मोन्नतिरपि ॥ ६२-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pariprītā yātāḥ khalu bhavadupētā vrajajuṣō
vrajaṁ yāvattāvannijamakhavibhaṅgaṁ niśamayan |
bhavantaṁ jānannapyadhikarajasā:’:’krāntahr̥dayō
na sēhē dēvēndrastvaduparacitātmōnnatirapi || 62-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Indra got the message that yagnya offering to him was prevented by Krishna. Even though, he was aware who Krishna was and he knew that it was through His grace, Indra  got high position among Devas, but still unable to overcome the rajo guna of his mind, Indra got furious.

stanzas.sanskrit:
मनुष्यत्वं यातो मधुभिदपि देवेष्वविनयं
विधत्ते चेन्नष्टस्त्रिदशसदसां कोऽपि महिमा ।
ततश्च ध्वंसिष्ये पशुपहतकस्य श्रियमिति
प्रवृत्तस्त्वां जेतुं स किल मघवा दुर्मदनिधिः ॥ ६२-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
manuṣyatvaṁ yātō madhubhidapi dēvēṣvavinayaṁ
vidhattē cēnnaṣṭastridaśasadasāṁ kō:’pi mahimā |
tataśca dhvaṁsiṣyē paśupahatakasya śriyamiti
pravr̥ttastvāṁ jētuṁ sa kila maghavā durmadanidhiḥ || 62-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Indra was full of pride and set out to win Krishna. He reasoned that even if it was Lord Vishnu himself, in human form, if he shows disrespect to Gods, what ever their prestige, would be lost. So he made up his mind to destroy Krishna and all his prosperity.

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वदावासं हन्तुं प्रलयजलदानम्बरभुवि
प्रहिण्वन् बिभ्राणः कुलिशमयमभ्रेभगमनः ।
प्रतस्थेऽन्यैरन्तर्दहनमरुदाद्यैर्विहसितो
भवन्माया नैव त्रिभुवनपते मोहयति कम् ॥ ६२-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadāvāsaṁ hantuṁ pralayajaladānaṁbarabhuvi
prahiṇvan bibhrāṇaḥ kuliśamayamabhrēbhagamanaḥ |
pratasthē:’nyairantardahanamarudādyairvihasitō
bhavanmāyā naiva tribhuvanapatē mōhayati kam || 62-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: He released heavy rain causing clouds along with thunder and came riding on airavat elephant with the thunderbolt in hand, followed by agni and vaayu. Bhattathiri wondered at the way the Bhagwan's maya caused affliction of mind.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सुरेन्द्रः क्रुद्धश्चेद्द्विजकरुणया शैलकृपया-
प्यनातङ्कोऽस्माकं नियत इति विश्वास्य पशुपान् ।
अहो किं नायातो गिरिभिदिति सञ्चिन्त्य निवसन्
मरुद्गेहाधीश प्रणुद मुरवैरिन् मम गदान् ॥ ६२-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
surēndraḥ kruddhaścēdvijakaruṇayā śailakr̥payā-
pyanātaṅkō:’smākaṁ niyata iti viśvāsya paśupān |
ahō kiṁ nāyātō giribhiditi sañcintya nivasan
marudgēhādhīśa praṇuda muravairin mama gadān || 62-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Seeing the rain clouds, Gopas became scared. Krishna convinced them that Indra's anger will not cause any destruction to Gokula. They have the mercy of the Brahmins and Govardhana hill which will surely protect them. 
 Krishna waited for the arrival of Indra. 
Bhattathiri  requested Lord Guruvayoorappan, slayer of Mura, to eradicate his ailments and protect him.
